subject: Marketloom renewal: scale benchmarking and term/upsell proposal
messages:
From: Jonah Price <jonah.price@marketloom.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal cycle coming up — need a clear perf comparison

Kimberly,

We're coming up on our renewal and have an aggressive timeline. A competitor has approached us with a lower headline price and claims they can hit our peak inference needs. Before we decide, I need a concrete apples-to-apples comparison on latency tail, throughput at our profile, and cost per 1M tokens.

Can Redwood run a short benchmark using our public sample workload and provide a simple summary and a recommended committed capacity profile (and the pricing delta) that would keep us within our latency SLO?

If you can get results in the next 7 business days that would be ideal — our procurement window closes mid-November. Also copy Ayesha (CTO) and procurement as this will be a technical + commercial decision.

Thanks,
Jonah
Head of Infrastructure
Marketloom
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonah Price <jonah.price@marketloom.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal cycle coming up — need a clear perf comparison

Jonah — thanks for the note and the heads-up on timing. We can absolutely run an apples-to-apples perf run and a short bakeoff. Action items I propose: 

1) You send a representative workload (sample request traces + average payload size + 95th/99th payload sizes).
2) We run two scenarios: a) shared-hosted (current plan) with prefix caching and optimized quantization; b) Dedicated pool sized to your 95th-percentile QPS with a 20% buffer.
3) We produce: latency p50/p95/p99, sustained throughput, cost per 1M tokens for both scenarios, and a simple ops runbook for failover.

If that works I can loop in our infra engineer to run the bench and get a draft mutual action plan to you by Tuesday. Separately, we can present a 12-month committed pricing option that includes a Dedicated capacity discount and an uptime SLA.

Two quick asks: who should we put on the technical kickoff (email addresses) and does procurement require SOC 2 evidence or a security questionnaire up front?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@marketloom.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Jonah Price <jonah.price@marketloom.com>, procurement@marketloom.com
Date: Sat, 4 Nov 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal cycle coming up — need a clear perf comparison

Kim — thanks. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Target steady-state: 1,200 requests/sec average during peak window, 1.8k burst. Typical input size: 512 tokens median; 95th ~ 1500 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for single-turn completions.
- Key evaluation: we care about sustained throughput under concurrency and p99 tail under cold-start. Competitor quoted a ~25% lower cost but couldn't validate p99.

Procurement: yes, we need SOC 2 Type II and an updated security questionnaire. If you can attach SOC 2 evidence with the bench that would accelerate the commercial review.

I'll send a brief sample trace by EOD. Please include a proposed term: 12 vs 24 months with committed throughput and the impact on unit cost.

—Ayesha
CTO, Marketloom
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@marketloom.com>, Jonah Price <jonah.price@marketloom.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal cycle coming up — need a clear perf comparison

Ayesha / Jonah — thanks for the sample traces. We completed a targeted benchmark run on 1 Nov and are attaching the summary and raw results. Highlights below (full results attached as marketloom_benchmark_results_20281101.xlsx):

- Shared-hosted (optimized): p50 18ms, p95 103ms, p99 187ms; sustained throughput up to ~850 rps before latency degradation. Cost estimate: $1,280 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated pool (recommended sizing: 2x g4p-equivalent nodes, committed throughput target ~1,500 rps): p50 12ms, p95 68ms, p99 112ms; sustained throughput 1,600 rps. Cost estimate (12-mo commit): $980 per 1M tokens.

Interpretation: Dedicated gives you headroom for peak and the p99 headroom to meet the 120ms SLO. The competitor's price delta appears attractive but their config was not tested for p99 under your trace; we included a side-by-side latency profile in the workbook.

Attachments & links:
- marketloom_benchmark_results_20281101.xlsx (detailed graphs and raw traces)
- marketloom_mutual_action_plan_20281104.pdf (proposed dates, responsibilities and procurement milestones)
- redwood_scope_and_pricing_20281106.pdf (12-mo and 24-mo committed pricing tiers; includes Dedicated pool discount)
- Drive link: https://redwood.app/drive/marketloom-bench-20281101
- HubSpot:HS-22478 (deal record with pricing scenarios)

Next steps I propose: 
- If procurement confirms SOC 2 is sufficient, we can fast-track a 12-month committed deal with a 10% commit discount and a 30% uplift credit if you exceed baseline throughput.
- Technical follow-up: 45-minute review with our infra team to walk through p99 behavior and the failover runbook. 

Available times: Wed 11/8 09:00-12:00 PST or Thu 11/9 13:00-16:00 PST. Please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: procurement@marketloom.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Jonah Price <jonah.price@marketloom.com>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@marketloom.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal cycle coming up — need a clear perf comparison

Kim — thanks for the quick turn and the attachments. Procurement will review SOC 2 evidence and the mutual action plan today. The technical team will join the 45-minute review — please book Wed 11/8 09:30 PST and include the infra runbook itemized in the MAP.

Commercial note: our budget team prefers a 24-month commitment if the unit economics move below $1,000 per 1M tokens; please include the 24-month pricing page in the DocuSign packet. We'll aim to have internal approval by 11/17.

Procurement Team
Marketloom
